title: [28/9/2024] The percentage of people visiting a museum at least once a year
prompt: The graph below shows the percentage of people visiting a museum at least once a year between 1980 and 2010. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph gives information about the proportion of visitors of different age groups going to museums at least once per year from 1980 to 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, in the first decade, the popularity of visiting museums among the 15-24 and 50+ age groups increased, while it declined among those aged 25-49, but after 1990, these trends reversed for all age groups. Moreover, the over 50s were the most likely to visit the museum museum, and the youngest group were the least likely, with the latter experiencing a slight net increase over the period.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the youngest and oldest age brackets, in 1980, around 48% of the latter visited museums annually, more than double the former’s 20%. Subsequently, visitor numbers of the older group underwent a slight increase to 50% by 1990, before gradually declining to just over 40% in the final year. In contrast, there was a moderate growth seen in the younger group, with its numbers reaching a high of 25% in 1990, and remaining around that level until 2005, before ending up at 22% by 2010.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining groups, after starting the period with around 36% of both 15-24- and 25-34-year-olds going once or more a year, declines were seen until 1990, when around 28% of people in both age groups did so. Then, both witnessed a notable recovery, with the former’s numbers bouncing back to the initial level by 1995 and slightly declining to 34% by 2010, while those for the older group rebounded more strongly before also steadily decreasing to 37% by the end of the period.
